editorial_master_copy.headline: India's semiconductor build-out is producing commercial evidence. But not every layer is equally real yet.
body: India now has multiple semiconductor facilities in commercial production, while the country's first major front-end wafer fab remains under construction.
At the same time, a new wave of agreements is assembling around equipment, materials, packaging, logistics and supplier localisation.
EMRADAR keeps those signals separate rather than treating them as one completed ecosystem.

Commercial production is evidence. An MoU is evidence of intent. Planned capacity is not operating capacity. The next test is whether supplier commitments become installed capacity, orders, revenue and repeat demand.
That progression—not the number of announcements—is what EMRADAR will track.

adaptation_stage.principle: One editorial master; destination-native insertions. Preserve FORMING and commercial-proof distinction.

assets.copy:
India's semiconductor build-out is producing commercial evidence. But not every layer is equally real yet.

EMRADAR currently classifies the INDIA SEMICONDUCTOR ECOSYSTEM as FORMING.

The distinction matters:

Commercial production is evidence.
An MoU is evidence of intent.
Planned capacity is not operating capacity.

The next test is whether supplier commitments progress through:
CAPACITY → ORDERS → REVENUE → REPEAT DEMAND.

Rather than counting semiconductor announcements, EMRADAR will track which parts of the ecosystem actually cross into commercial proof—and which do not.

India's semiconductor ecosystem is FORMING. The useful question now isn't how many projects are announced, but which layers become commercially real.

EMRADAR is tracking:
commitment → capacity → orders → revenue → repeat demand.

Planned capacity ≠ operating capacity.

assets.subject: Contribution idea: measuring when India's semiconductor ecosystem becomes commercially real
assets.copy:
EMRADAR is tracking India's semiconductor ecosystem as a FORMING market, but with a distinction that gets lost when announcements, MoUs, planned capacity and commercial production are grouped together.

A proposed contribution would map the ecosystem by evidence state—commitment, installed capacity, commercial orders, revenue and repeat demand—and identify what would need to happen for the formation to strengthen or weaken.

The aim is not another overview of India's semiconductor ambitions, but a measurable framework for following which layers are becoming economically real.

INDIA SEMICONDUCTOR ECOSYSTEM — FORMING

Commercial activity is emerging across parts of India's semiconductor build-out, while other layers remain at agreement, planned-capacity or construction stage.

EMRADAR tracks the progression:
ANNOUNCEMENT → COMMITMENT → CAPACITY → ORDERS → REVENUE → REPEAT DEMAND

Next evidence: supplier capacity coming online, commercial orders, disclosed revenue exposure and repeat demand.

Falsification: repeated delays, cancelled commitments, capacity without utilisation, or supplier economics failing to materialise.
